newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bourse raps 3 Scotts directors.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bourse raps 3 Scotts directors.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) issued a stinging criticism of three directors of Scotts Holdings Ltd on Thursday, saying they should not serve as directors on any other listed companies.

The SES said in a statement that Ameerali R Jumabhoy, Rafiq Jumabhoy and Iqbal Jamabhoy had failed to ensure that a majority of the company's board were independent directors as requested by the SES more than three months ago.
In March, the SES had separately reprimanded the three directors for a misstatement in a 1991 prospectus ahead of the listing of the company on the exchange and for other breaches of SES rules.

Scotts, a diversified property and leisure company, is majority owned by the Jumabhoy family but has suffered over the last year from a marathon battle between various family members for control of the company.
The SES said the long-term interest of the company and its minority shareholders would suffer unless a majority of the board were independent.
"The exchange views with serious concern that the disputes among the Jumabhoy directors have detracted (sic) them from their primary duty to the company," it said.

"In view of the abovementioned failure, and the breaches of listing requirements and the misstatement in prospectus set out in the SES' statement of March 19, 1997, the exchange considers that it would not be appropriate for (the three) to act as directors of listed companies other than (Scotts)."
